ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the circuit there is power supply E1, and the polarity shown in the figure indicates that its upper terminal is negative and its lower terminal is positive; the lower common wire is connected to point B. R1=2 kΩ is connected from the upper terminal of E1 to the node at the left end of the diode, and R2=2 kΩ is connected from this node to the lower common node. The diode is in the middle, and its right end is connected to point A. In the right branch, point A is connected through R3=4 kΩ to the upper terminal of power supply E2; E2 is labeled 3 V, and its upper terminal is positive while its lower terminal is connected to common node B. Reasoning: Take point B as 0 V. Since E1=4 V and its upper terminal is negative and its lower terminal is connected to B, the potential of the upper terminal of E1 is -4 V. First assume the ideal diode is cut off; then the left node is divided by equal R1 and R2 between -4 V and 0 V, and its potential is -2 V. On the right side, because the diode is cut off, there is no current in R3, so the potential of point A equals the potential of the upper terminal of E2, namely +3 V. According to the diode direction in the figure, it will conduct only when the left-end potential is higher than point A; now the left end -2 V is lower than point A +3 V, so the cutoff assumption is self-consistent. Therefore U_AB=V_A−V_B=3−0=3 V.

raw_record.question_text: Question: In the circuit shown in figure, the diode is an ideal component. When \( E1 = 4V \), \( U_{AB} = \) ________ V.

method.method_draft: Take B as 0 V. From the image polarity, the upper terminal of E1 is -4 V when E1=4 V, while B is 0 V. If the diode is open, the left diode terminal is the midpoint of equal 2 kΩ resistors between -4 V and 0 V, so it is -2 V. On the right, with the diode open there is no current in R3, so A is at the top of E2, namely +3 V. Since the diode as drawn would conduct only if the left terminal were higher than A, but -2 V is lower than +3 V, the open state is self-consistent. Therefore U_AB=V_A-V_B=3 V.

method.method_draft: Assume first that the ideal diode conducts, so the left diode node and A are shorted to one common voltage V. With B=0 V, the image polarities give the R1 endpoint at -4 V, R2 endpoint at 0 V, and the R3 lower-source endpoint at +3 V. Apply KCL at the common node: (V+4)/2k + V/2k + (V-3)/4k = 0, giving V=-1 V. At V=-1 V, the right branch through R3 supplies current from the +3 V source into the node, so the current needed through the diode is from the A/right side toward the left side. That is opposite the allowed direction shown by the diode symbol, so the conducting assumption is invalid. Thus the diode is off; then no current flows through R3 and A remains at +3 V, so U_AB=3 V.
method.CoT_raw:
图像描述：电路底部是一条公共节点，右侧标为 B，可取 B=0 V；右上端为 A，箭头标出 U_AB 是从 A 到 B 的电压。左侧电源 E1 的极性在图中显示为下端为正、上端为负；E1 上端通过 R1=2 kΩ 接到中间左节点，该节点还通过 R2=2 kΩ 接到底部节点。中间左节点与右侧 A 节点之间接有一个理想二极管，二极管符号允许的正向电流方向为由左向右。右支路中，A 节点通过 R3=4 kΩ 接到电源 E2 的上端，E2=3 V 且上端为正、下端接到底部 B 节点。

推理：先假设理想二极管导通，则二极管两端短接，中间左节点与 A 节点为同一电位 V。取 B=0 V。由图中极性可知：E1=4 V 且下正上负，所以 R1 左端电位为 -4 V；R2 下端为 0 V；E2 上端为 +3 V。对公共节点列 KCL：
(V+4)/2k + V/2k + (V-3)/4k = 0。
两边乘以 4k 得 2(V+4)+2V+(V-3)=0，即 5V+5=0，所以 V=-1 V。
在 V=-1 V 时，右支路 R3 中电流按从节点流向 +3 V 端计算为 (V-3)/4k=-1 mA，说明实际电流由 +3 V 电源经 R3 流入 A 节点。左侧网络在该节点需要的净电流为 (V+4)/2k + V/2k = 1 mA，因此二极管中所需电流方向为从右侧 A 节点流向左侧节点。这与图中二极管允许的左向右导通方向相反，所以“二极管导通”的假设不成立。
因此二极管截止。截止后右侧支路与左侧断开，R3 中没有电流，R3 上无压降，所以 A 点电位等于 E2 上端电位 +3 V。B 点为 0 V，因此 U_AB=V_A−V_B=3 V。

On the right side, because the diode is cut off, there is no current in R3, so the potential of point A equals the potential of the upper terminal of E2, namely +3 V. According to the diode direction in the figure, it will conduct only when the left-end potential is higher than point A; now the left end -2 V is lower than point A +3 V, so the cutoff assumption is self-consistent. Therefore U_AB=V_A−V_B=3−0=3 V.
